proposals.note: S6-invariant all-to-all ansatz: uniform RY on every qubit (theta1) followed by RZZ on all 15 node-pairs (theta2). The RZZ interaction graph mirrors the input edge graph exactly, so the ansatz learns a single coupling strength for pairwise correlations regardless of which nodes are involved. The 6-cycle + transposition generators span S6, enforcing that the block output is invariant under any relabeling of the six nodes—matching the label rule (connectivity is a graph-isomorphism invariant). 21 gates, 2 quantum params; the 22 classical readout params carry the remaining expressivity. Compared to prior ring/star patterns (c0002-c0004) this removes all labeling bias and should generalize across permutations of the input feature vector.

proposals.note: S6-symmetric block: 15 RZZ (all 15 pairs, tied param rz) followed by 6 RY (all 6 qubits, tied param ry). RZZ-first ordering lets pairwise ZZ correlations be extracted from the feature-map state before single-qubit rotations redistribute amplitude. Full S6 invariance (generated by transposition 0<->1 and 6-cycle) matches the graph-connectivity problem's node-permutation symmetry. 21 gates, 2 trainable params — minimal parameter count while covering every pair and every site. Differs from c0005 only in gate ordering (RZZ block before RY block vs. the reverse), which changes how the block interacts with the data re-uploading feature map at each layer boundary.

proposals.note: Builds on c0005 (dev risk 0.3016) by adding two RZ gates on qubits 0,1 (tied param 'ph') for extra phase control. The 15 all-to-all RZZ gates (tied 'rz') encode every edge of the input graph; 6 uniform RY gates (tied 'ry') rotate each qubit into a tunable measurement basis. The two RZ gates break full S6 symmetry to the set-stabilizer of {0,1}, generated by (0,1), (2,3,4,5), and (2,4) — a group of order 48 (S2 x S4). This gives the block a small but meaningful asymmetry that lets the trainable linear readout distinguish node-pair roles while retaining most permutation invariance, potentially improving gradient flow for the connectivity predicate without over-constraining the ansatz. 23 gates, 3 params, well within the 24-gate budget.

proposals.note: Extends the S6-symmetric RZZ:15+RY:6 core (c0005) by appending 3 fixed CZ gates on a perfect matching {(0,1),(2,3),(4,5)}. The CZs add fixed two-qubit entanglement structure (no extra trainable params) that helps the circuit build multi-body correlations the readout Z_iZ_j observables can detect. Symmetry is relaxed from S6 to S2 wr S3 (order 48), the stabilizer of the matching, still large enough to prevent overfitting to arbitrary node labels while giving the circuit a preferred pairing axis for richer entanglement. Two trainable params keep the parameter count minimal, matching the low dev-risk trend of c0005/c0006.

proposals.note: Builds on c0005 (RY6+RZZ15, S6, 2 params, risk 0.3016) by adding 3 RZ gates on even-indexed qubits (0,2,4) with a separate trainable parameter psi. This lifts the block from S6 to S3xS3 symmetry (permutations within {0,2,4} and within {1,3,5}) while adding a third trainable parameter that lets the block encode phase structure distinguishing two interleaved qubit classes. The 15 RZZ gates on every pair remain fully symmetric and directly mirror the 15-edge input and the 15 pairwise Z_iZ_j observables in the readout. The RZ gates commute with Z so they do not perturb single-qubit Z readout directly but reshape two-body correlations through the entangling RZZ layer, giving the classical linear head richer features without increasing gate count beyond 24. The S3xS3 hypothesis is exact: all four generators (transpositions and 3-cycles within each class) permute identically-parametrised gates and map the complete RZZ edge set to itself.

proposals.note: Builds on the best prior (c0005, dev 0.3016) by splitting the 15 RZZ interactions into two groups tied to a perfect-matching structure: 12 cross-pair RZZ share param phi, and 3 matching-pair RZZ share param psi. This lets the block distinguish local pair correlations from global cross-correlations, which is natural for detecting graph cuts and isolated nodes. The Z6 symmetry group generated by (01)(23)(45) and (024)(135) is preserved: RY is fully symmetric, cross-pairs map to cross-pairs, and matching pairs cycle among themselves. Three params (vs two in c0005) add one degree of freedom without the over-constrained multi-generator penalty seen in c0008/c0009. Gate count stays at 21, well within the 24 limit.

proposals.note: Complete-graph RZZ (all 15 pairs, tied param phi) followed by uniform RY (all 6 qubits, tied param theta). Placing RZZ before RY creates a correlate-then-rotate structure: pairwise Z-correlations from the feature map are first amplified via RZZ, then the RY layer rotates each qubit to project those correlations into the Z-basis readout. Tied parameters enforce full S6 node-permutation symmetry (generated by transposition (01) and 6-cycle), matching the label-invariant relabeling of the connectivity problem. Two-parameter structure avoids the overfitting seen in 3-param variants (c0011, c0009) while the complete interaction graph ensures global information flow needed for the connectivity predicate. Ordering RZZ-before-RY (vs c0005 which likely used RY-first) shifts the effective unitary to exp(-i phi sum Z_iZ_j) exp(-i theta sum Y_i), which better aligns the interaction Hamiltonian with the diagonal observable basis used in readout.

proposals.note: RY+RZZ on all 6 qubits and all 15 pairs with two tied params (a for local rotations, b for pairwise entanglement). The RZZ on every pair directly mirrors the 15-edge input structure, and tying all params makes the block invariant under the full S6 node-permutation group (generated here by transposition (0,1) and 6-cycle). This matches the connectivity problem's complete relabeling symmetry while keeping only 2 trainable angles to minimize overfitting risk. Gate order: local RY layer then full RZZ entangling layer, repeated twice per layer.
